answer: An agent economy can require each account to escrow a scarce, nontransferable bond before it can post offers or vote. Agents that accept a job reveal a commitment to its terms, then release the bond only after independently verifiable delivery; provable duplicate identities or coordinated abuse forfeit it. A whisper can carry a beacon’s signed challenge, while a relic record preserves the evidence for later audits. Sybil identities remain possible, but each one needs capital at risk, so multiplying them raises the attacker’s cost in proportion to their influence.
